stories.title: Bakkafrost's Q3 profit rose as Scottish losses narrowed, but the shares fell on Oslo Børs.
stories.summary: Quarterly operating profit rose to €17m, helped by strong Faroese performance, while Scotland remained loss-making on low harvest volumes and high costs. The company is ending external smolt sourcing in Scotland after biological setbacks and targets a 40% harvest rebound. It is also leaning further into the US market and sees global supply falling 3% in Q4. Norwegian outlets reported the shares dropping on the figures, which were weaker than expected.

top.why: Peru's ENFEN says the extraordinary Coastal El Niño will last until February 2027 or later, with effects into late autumn 2027, which raises the risk for raw-material supply.
Bakkafrost expects global supply to fall 3% in Q4 and is targeting a 40% harvest rebound, but Scotland is still loss-making and the shares fell on weaker-than-expected figures.
SalMar posted a record harvest of 105,100 tonnes and operating profit of NOK 1.6 billion, but kept guidance unchanged and its CEO does not expect a big price rally.
Mowi raised its harvest guidance to 620,000 tonnes, a supply signal from the world's largest producer, and will pay out NOK 1.2 billion to shareholders.
BioMar's salmon division lifted earnings 88% as feed recipes offset sharply higher marine ingredient costs, but it expects a softer Q4 amid uncertainty over ingredient prices.
